stemMd: A photosynthesising plant is given water containing a labelled oxygen isotope. Where can the label appear directly during the light-dependent reactions?

options.label: C
options.textMd: Only in the carbon atoms of glucose

options.label: D
options.textMd: Nowhere, because water is not involved

explanationMd: The oxygen released during oxygenic photosynthesis comes from water splitting. Isotope tracing distinguishes this source from carbon dioxide without changing the chemical identity of the oxygen atom.

distractorRationale.e: Chemical reactions do not turn oxygen into magnesium.
distractorRationale.b: Photosynthesis does not split water to make nitrogen.
distractorRationale.c: An oxygen isotope cannot become carbon chemically.
distractorRationale.d: Water supplies electrons in oxygenic photosynthesis.
